market_question: Will Renan Santos finish in second place in the first round of the 2026 Brazilian presidential election?
reasoning: Renan Santos is a low-profile federal deputy with minimal national name recognition and no plausible path to finishing second in a presidential field dominated by major figures like Lula, Tarcísio de Freitas, and Romeu Zema. Even if he runs, his vote share would be negligible. The market-implied 7.3% probability is absurdly high relative to his realistic chances, which are closer to 0.05%.
evidence_points: No current polling shows Renan Santos as a competitive candidate for top-two finish; he is not mentioned in any credible election surveys.
In 2022, the second-place finisher was Jair Bolsonaro (43.2%), and the third-place candidate Simone Tebet had only 4.2%; a minor deputy would be far behind.
MDB, his party, is more likely to field a centrist candidate like Simone Tebet rather than an obscure deputy, and Santos lacks executive experience or national campaign infrastructure.
sources_consulted: General awareness of current Brazilian political figures and 2026 candidate speculation (e.g., Tarcísio de Freitas, Romeu Zema, Simone Tebet)
